name: ophcrack
desc: Microsoft Windows password cracker using rainbow tables
why: Rainbow table password cracker that shows how Windows LM and NTLM hashes actually get attacked; a clear window into authentication weakness.

brief.what_it_is: Ophcrack is a free, GPL-licensed Windows password cracker that uses rainbow tables. It takes password hashes (LM and NTLM) and looks them up against precomputed tables to recover the original passwords. It ships with a graphical interface and runs on Windows, Linux/Unix and Mac OS X. The site also offers free tables for Windows XP and Vista/7, plus a LiveCD that boots and cracks without installation. Its feature list includes a brute-force module for simple passwords, an audit mode with CSV export, real-time graphs, and the ability to load hashes from an encrypted SAM recovered from a Windows partition.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a very efficient implementation of rainbow tables, built by the inventors of the method. Its purpose is to demonstrate and exploit how weak Windows password hashing is in practice.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the mechanism in detail. It says the tool is based on rainbow tables and that the tables cover specific charsets and password patterns, such as dictionary-plus-suffix sets, length-limited full charsets, and numeric-only sets. The tables are precomputed and downloaded separately, and the XP tables target LM hashes while the Vista/7 tables target NT hashes.
brief.install_notes: The brief's install path is brew install ophcrack. Beyond that, the site offers a Windows portable zip (ophcrack-3.8.0-bin.zip, supports Windows 2000 through 10), a source tarball (ophcrack-3.8.0.tar.bz2), and a LiveCD ISO that needs no installation. Three LiveCD variants exist: XP (LM hashes), Vista/7 (NT hashes), and a no-tables build. Rainbow tables are a separate download: the free XP set totals 17.0GB, the free Vista set 11.9GB, and the professional Vista set 2.3TB, all distributed largely via torrent. The site lists md5sums for every file.
brief.standout: Ophcrack is a long-lived, open reference for attacking the LM and NTLM hashes that Windows has used for decades, so it is a concrete demonstration of authentication weakness. Its tables are published openly with stated success rates and charset details, which makes it easy to see exactly what coverage each set provides.
brief.status: The download page says the latest version is 3.8.0 and the LiveCD is at 3.6.0, so the project is still being published. I found no release date or commit history on the pages I read, so I cannot give a firm last-release date. Treat it as maintained by the site's own account, but unverified beyond that.
brief.caveats: The XP tables cannot crack Vista or 7 passwords, and the Vista tables cannot crack XP (LM) passwords. The table downloads are very large, and the professional Vista set is 2.3TB, offered only as a torrent. The brute-force module is described only for simple passwords. The site's table success rates are as stated by the authors and I did not verify them. The site does not state platform-specific install steps for macOS or Linux. Mac OS X is listed under platforms, but I saw no Mac build on the download page, only Windows and source.
quotes: Ophcrack is a free Windows password cracker based on rainbow tables.
It is a very efficient implementation of rainbow tables done by the inventors of the method.
